lines.li: [them,their:tribal] The fields gave you their food, the spirits must be pleased with you.
[them,their:medieval] Harvest in, then, that's a good week for any village.
[them] I hear you've brought a harvest in.
[us] Most of it, anyway.
[them] That's the best news a colony can have.
[them,their:empire] Your council has decreed {DECREE}, I understand.
[them] Word is your council settled on {DECREE}.
[us,us:speaker] It came across my table, yes.
[us] It did, for now.
[them] Every place has its rules, and yours seem fair enough.
[them] Someone said your people have worked out {RESEARCH}.
[us] We have, after a lot of argument.
[them,their:spacer,!their:empire] Every world gets there in the end.
[them,their:tribal] New knowledge, and old knowledge forgotten, that is the way of it.
[them] Knowing a thing is half of having it.
[them] How goes {PROJECT}?
[us] Slowly, but it goes.
[them] That's how the big ones always go.
[them] {NEWCOMER} is new here, isn't that right?
[us] Settling in, slowly.
[them,their:tribal] A new face at the fire is a blessing.
[them] New blood keeps a place alive.
[them] It's been quiet out your way, by the look of it.
[us] Don't say that, you'll bring something down on us.
[them,their:tribal] Then I'll unsay it, and the spirits didn't hear.
[them] I'll knock on wood for you.
[them] Is something on today, the place feels different?
[us] It's {DAY}.
[them,their:tribal] Then my feet brought me on a good day.
[them] Then I've come on a good day.
[them] I'm told I just missed {DAY}.
[us] There's always next year.
[them] I'll plan the road better.
[them] Machines came at you, I hear.
[us] They did, and we're still here.
[them,their:tribal] The dead iron walks, and you stood against it.
[them] Nobody I know likes fighting those.
[them] Insects out of the ground, is that true?
[us] It was, and I'd rather not talk about it.
[them] I'd sleep with one eye open after that.
[them] Beasts came for you, I heard.
[us] They did.
[them,their:tribal] When the beasts turn on people, something is wrong in the land.
[them] The land out here doesn't love anyone.
[them] I hear your people chose {SPEAKER} to speak for them.
[us,us:speaker] They did, and I'm still getting used to it.
[us] They did.
[them,their:empire] A voice chosen by the people, how unusual.
[them] Choosing is better than being chosen for.
[them] We've eaten at the same table, you and I.
[us] We have, and we will again.
[them,their:tribal] Then we are bound a little, by the old way.
[them] Then you're more than a stranger to me.
[them] Have you kept practicing what I showed you?
[us] Every day I can.
[us] Not as much as I should.
[them] It comes, with practice.
[them] Our bout's been on my mind, you fight better than you look.
[us] I'll take that as praise.
[them] It was meant as one.
[them] I've been thinking about what you said, about faith.
[us] And?
[them,samefaith] And it's good to be reminded by someone who keeps it too.
[them] And I'm still thinking.
[them] Your letter to {WROTE} is on its way, I'm told.
[us] Thank you for seeing to it.
[them] Letters are what keep this frontier from being lonely.
[them,their:empire] You lead here, I'm told, so I will speak plainly.
[them] So you're the one they listen to.
[us] Some days.
[them] That's every leader I've known.
[them] You're the healer here, aren't you?
[us] I do what I can.
[them,their:tribal] Then the spirits work through your hands.
[them] Then I know who to find if the road goes badly.
[them] You've seen a few winters out here.
[us] More than I'd like to count.
[them,their:tribal] The old ones are the memory of a people.
[them] And still working, I see.
[them] You're new here too, aren't you?
[us] Is it that obvious?
[them] You still look at everything.
[them] How's {OURCHILD} doing?
[us] Growing faster than I can keep up with.
[them,them:parent] Mine too, they never stop.
[them] That's how it should be.
[us] You've been on the road a long time, haven't you?
[them] Longer than you've been alive, I'd guess.
[us] What's the secret?
[them,their:tribal] Walk with the seasons, never against them.
[them] Keep walking, and never argue with the weather.
[us] Is someone waiting for you at home?
[them] {THEIRSPOUSE}, and they'll want to hear all about this place.
[us] Tell them we said hello.
[them] There's not a stick of firewood to spare at home.
[us] Is it that cold there?
[them,their:tribal] The cold sits on us like a hungry spirit, and the fires eat everything.
[them] Colder than it should be, and the wood went fast.
[them] We're short of hands at home, with the fighting.
[us] Who's working the fields?
[them] Whoever's left, and the old ones too.
[them] Some of ours are on the road this way with goods to sell.
[us] We'll be glad to see them.
[them,their:medieval] Have your silver counted, they drive a hard bargain.
[them] Have your silver ready, then.
[them] More of my people are coming this way, I'm told.
[us] They'll be welcome.
[them] I'll tell them you said so.
[them] The stores are lean at home this season.
[us] Is anyone going hungry?
[them] Not yet, the elders share it out carefully.
[them] {TOWN} has seen better years, the market's half empty.
[us] What would help?
[them] A good harvest, and fewer tax men.
[them] Money's tight in {TOWN} these days.
[us] Is it the roads, or the prices?
[them] Both, and everything else besides.
[us] How are things at your fires?
[them] The hunt feeds us and the elders argue, so all is as it should be.
[us] That sounds peaceful.
[them] Peace is mostly arguing that nobody wins.
[us] How's {TOWN} keeping?
[them] Steady, aye, the same fields and the same quarrels.
[us] Could be worse.
[them] It could, and I'll not complain.
[us] Is all well at home?
[them] All is as it should be, and the court sees that it stays so.
[us] Lucky you.
[them] Order is not luck, it is work.
[them] Our fires have never burned so many, the elders say.
[us] That's a fine thing to hear.
[them] It is, and they say it with worry, in case it doesn't last.
[them] {TOWN} has a new market hall going up, and the old one's still full.
[us] Business is good, then.
[them] Good enough that everyone's cousin wants to move there.
[them] {TOWN}'s growing so fast they can't build houses quick enough.
[us] There are worse problems.
[them] Tell that to the ones sleeping in the warehouses.
[them] This war with {WAR} has gone on too long.
[us] Is there no end in sight?
[them,their:tribal] Not until one side runs out of young ones to send.
[them] Not one I can see from here.
[them] We're at war with {WAR} now, did you hear?
[us] We heard, I'm sorry.
[them] So am I, it came too fast for anyone to stop it.
[them] Our people fought {WAR} on your land, I'm told, and I'm sorry for the trouble.
[us] It wasn't your doing.
[them] It was, a little.
[them] You're on good terms with {WAR}, I know.
[us] We're on good terms with most people.
[them] Then don't take sides, and we'll stay friends too.
[them] {BATTLEA} and {BATTLEB} fought on your land, I'm told.
[us] It was close enough to hear.
[them] Better to hear it than be in it.
[them] Fog like this, the road just disappears.
[us] Stay till it lifts.
[them] I mean to.
[them] Listen to that storm.
[us,tribal] The spirits are arguing again.
[us] It'll blow over.
[them] They always do, in the end.
[us] You're up early.
[them,their:medieval] A traveler's day starts before the cock crows.
[them,their:tribal] The day is best caught young.
[them] Road habits.
[us] Is there anything you need while you're with us?
[them] Nothing at all, you've been good hosts.
[us] Say so if that changes.
[us] How are you settling in?
[them] Better than I expected.
[us] Let us know if you need anything.
